# `silk/platform/native/descriptor`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Reads and writes on file descriptors that the caller owns, for native providers.

## When to use
Use [`NativeDescriptor`](#NativeDescriptor) to build a native provider, such as `silk.io.writer_native` or
`silk.io.standard_input_native`. Application code uses the `Writer` and `StandardInput` effects
instead.

## Details
One system call transfers at most 0x7ffff000 bytes. A call that a signal interrupts is made
again. An empty buffer makes no system call. The functions never close the descriptor.

## Errors
Each function returns `false` on failure and writes the native error code to `error`, or 0 when
the system returned a count that is not valid.

## Gotchas
- The caller keeps the descriptor open and controls access from other threads.
- [`NativeDescriptor.writeAll`](#NativeDescriptor.impl.writeAll) and [`NativeDescriptor.writeAllGather`](#NativeDescriptor.impl.writeAllGather) can fail after part of
  the bytes were written.
- The module is empty on targets other than Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc on x86_64
  or aarch64.

## Examples
### Make empty transfers
```silk
import silk.platform.native.descriptor { NativeDescriptor }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut nativeError = 0

  // Descriptor 1 is standard output. An empty write makes no system call.
  let written = run NativeDescriptor.writeAll(1, b"", &mut nativeError)
  if !written || nativeError != 0 {
    return 1
  }

  // A read of zero bytes also makes no system call.
  let mut empty: [u8; 0] = []
  let mut count: usize = 7
  let read = run NativeDescriptor.read(0, &mut empty, &mut count, &mut nativeError)
  if !read || count != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `NativeDescriptor` with `import silk.platform.native.descriptor { NativeDescriptor }`.

## `read`

```silk
pub unsafe extern "C" fn read(fd: i32, buffer: ?[*]mut u8, count: usize) -> isize
```

The C `read` function: reads at most `count` bytes from `fd` into `buffer`.

### Gotchas
`buffer` must have `count` writable bytes during the call. After a negative result, read the
error code at once.

<a id="write"></a>

## `write`

```silk
pub unsafe extern "C" fn write(fd: i32, buffer: ?[*]const u8, count: usize) -> isize
```

The C `write` function: writes at most `count` bytes from `buffer` to `fd`.

### Gotchas
`buffer` must have `count` readable bytes during the call. A positive result can be less than
`count`. After a negative result, read the error code at once.

## `NativeDescriptor`

```silk
pub struct NativeDescriptor
```

Safe reads and writes on a descriptor that the caller owns, for native providers.

### When to use
Use it to build a native provider, such as `silk.io.writer_native` or `silk.io.standard_input_native`.
Application code uses the `Writer` and `StandardInput` effects instead.

### Details
One system call transfers at most 0x7ffff000 bytes. A call that a signal interrupts is made
again. An empty buffer makes no system call. The functions never close the descriptor. Each
function returns `false` on failure and writes the native error code to `error`, or 0 when the
system returned a count that is not valid.

### Gotchas
- The caller keeps the descriptor open and controls access from other threads.
- The type is empty on targets other than Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc on x86_64
  or aarch64.

<a id="NativeDescriptor.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read(fd: i32, buffer: &mut [u8], count: &mut usize, error: &mut i32) -> bool
```

Reads one time from `fd` into the start of `buffer`, and returns whether it succeeded.

#### Details
On success, `count` is the number of bytes read. Zero means the end of input, or an empty
`buffer`. On failure, `count` is zero and `error` is the native error code, or zero for a
count that is not valid. Bytes after the count are not changed.

<a id="NativeDescriptor.impl.isTerminal"></a>

### Associated function `isTerminal`

```silk
pub effect fn isTerminal(fd: i32) -> bool
```

Returns whether `fd`, such as 2 for standard error, is a terminal. A closed descriptor, a
pipe, a file, or a failed query answers false.

<a id="NativeDescriptor.impl.writeAll"></a>

### Associated function `writeAll`

```silk
pub effect fn writeAll(fd: i32, buffer: &[u8], error: &mut i32) -> bool
```

Writes all of `buffer` to `fd`, and returns whether it succeeded.

#### Details
It calls `write` until all bytes are written. On failure, `error` is the native error code, or
zero if the system wrote nothing or returned a count that is not valid.

#### Gotchas
Part of `buffer` can be written before a failure. Do not write all of it again without a
check.

<a id="NativeDescriptor.impl.writeAllGather"></a>

### Associated function `writeAllGather`

```silk
pub effect fn writeAllGather(fd: i32, head: &[u8], rest: &[&[u8]], error: &mut i32) -> bool
```

Writes all of `head` and then all bytes of each slice of `rest` to `fd`, in order, and returns
whether it succeeded.

#### When to use
Use it to send buffered bytes and new slices together, without first copying the slices into
the buffer. Pass an empty `head` when there is no buffer.

#### Details
Each system call is one `writev` of at most eight non-empty slices and at most 0x7ffff000
bytes. After a partial write, the next call starts at the first byte that was not written.
Empty slices add nothing to a call. A call that a signal interrupts is made again. On failure,
`error` is the native error code, or zero if the system wrote nothing or returned a count that
is not valid.

#### Gotchas
Part of the bytes can be written before a failure. Do not write all of them again without a
check.
